question: [RE-3] on the rejected rows where the question is well posed
correction: An earlier run sampled the 1,659 rejected rows by a stride and reported that every measured row was UNREACHED. That was an artefact of the sample: the gate's atomic clause is near-collinear with a structural predicate on this corpus, so a stride lands almost surely in the degenerate slice. This run measures the rows where the question is well posed instead.
censoring_note: diabetes (18 rows) and pathfinder (9 rows) were not completed: these are by construction the instances on which the upward search must exhaust the up-set, and on those two networks a single instance outruns any budget we were willing to spend. They are censored, not dropped, and the finding below is a statement about the 30 attempted rows over four networks.
finding: The graded r_claim >= 2 stratum the gate discards is real but rare here. Of the 23 completed rows, 22 are UNREACHED and one -- sachs Erk->Akt at coverage 1.0, an 8-node component with k_g0 = 17 -- has r_hop = 5 and r_claim = 3, computed exactly in 0.23 s. The same pair has r_claim = 1 at coverages 0.5 and 0.25, so the clause is evaluated on the recovering set (coverage 1.0) and applied at all three.
assumption: UNREACHED is the retraction-only verdict and inherits Conjecture 2.
